hypotheses.justification: `hk₂` is implied by `hk₁` together with `le_hittingAfter (ω) : n ≤ hittingAfter u s n ω` (line 164 of the same file, in the same section and with the same `[ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder ι]` assumption, so no extra hypotheses are needed): from `hk₁ : k < hittingAfter u s n ω` we get `hk₁.le : k ≤ hittingAfter u s n ω`, hence `n ≤ k` by `le_trans (le_hittingAfter ω) hk₁.le` (this also covers the case `hittingAfter u s n ω = ⊤`, where `k ≤ ⊤` holds trivially). The proof then goes through verbatim, merely replacing both occurrences of `hk₂` by this derived `hnk : n ≤ k`: `have hnk : n ≤ k := le_trans (le_hittingAfter ω) hk₁.le; refine fun h ↦ not_le.2 hk₁ ?_; rw [hittingAfter, ite_eq_left ⟨k, hnk, h⟩]; exact_mod_cast csInf_le (s := {i | n ≤ i ∧ u i ω ∈ s}) ⟨n, fun j hj => hj.1⟩ ⟨hnk, h⟩`. So the statement `k < hittingAfter u s n ω → u k ω ∉ s` is true without `n ≤ k`, and `hk₂` can be deleted (the only other arguments it could interact with are `u`, `s`, `n`, `k`, `ω`, all of which it leaves untouched). The instance `[ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder ι]` cannot be deleted, since `hittingAfter` is only defined for a `Preorder`/`InfSet` and `csInf_le` is used, and `(hk₁ : k < hittingAfter u s n ω)` cannot be deleted either, since without it the claim is plainly false (take `k` with `u k ω ∈ s`, e.g. `k = n`).
